title: rule node
description:
One falsifiable condition. Which ddd it takes matters: an `invariant` must hold at all times inside one aggregate boundary and is enforced rather than checked; a `domain-rule` constrains what is allowed without being a transactional invariant; a `policy` is a decision the business could change, and a policy named as an invariant is how a business decision becomes something nobody feels able to change; a `specification` is a reusable predicate that selects instances; a `quality-attribute` is a non-functional constraint nevertheless specific to this domain.

A rule states the condition and carries an expression or examples — a rule with neither cannot become a test.

**A rule declares what it constrains.** The relationship between a rule and its subject is an edge, in `depends_on`, and not a sentence in the rationale: a relationship that exists only in prose is not in the network, and a reader tracing what a rule reaches will not arrive by the graph.

statement.description: The rule in prose, non-generative, and never the only place a fact a machine reads appears.

expression.description: The rule stated so a consumer can evaluate it. The grammar is deferred: it must be closed, total, side-effect free, and restricted to attributes reachable from the rule's boundary, and it arrives with the first consumer that evaluates one.

examples.description: Given/when/then cases a conformance test is derived from. Carried when `expression` is absent, and permitted alongside it. Where the material gives cases, both sides of the condition are recorded — a case that holds and a case that does not.

consistency.description: Whether this rule holds inside one transaction or converges after it. Required of a rule that reaches outside its own aggregate, which no single file can see — `src/claude/bin/check_knowledge.py` decides it.

x-alternation: Every field this kind requires is alternated separately against a gap naming that field, so a gap about one fact never excuses the absence of another. The shape is stated once in `../tables/invariants.json#/x-gap-alternation`. A prohibition is not excused: a gap says a fact is absent and cannot make a forbidden field allowed.
x-open: `depends_on` is listed as declared because a rule that names nothing it constrains leaves the relationship in prose. `domain-object/1` requires no such edge of a rule, and no shipped check reports its absence.

allOf.description: A rule with neither an expression nor examples cannot become a test. Either side may be what is missing, so a gap naming either is what says which.
